verdict: READY TO MERGE - 9 of 9 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: The new plan_live tests are behavioral: they use real receipts, ledger entries, plan JSON and pages under tmp_path, with no stubs around sourced_plans or refresh_live.
test_other_paths_feed_no_plan covers the negative boundaries well: a nested receipt, a skill freeze ledger, live.js itself, the PIP page, planned tests and a different plans root.
refresh_live has four tested outcomes: rebuilt, skipped for sealed records or a missing page (parametrized), skipped when the plan file is gone, and PlanError when the ledger has no entries.
The attach integration tests run the real script against a make_project repository with a git worktree and cover the staged, --committed and --continue paths.

test_a_move_that_lands_no_plan_file_rebuilds_nothing can fail: plan 0001 is a frozen receipts plan with a page, so rebuilding every plan unconditionally would break it. The committed test also asserts that plan 0001 is not rebuilt.

The failed-rebuild test checks the warning line, the exit code 0, that the receipt is staged in the target and that the worktree is removed, which pins the rule that a warning never turns into a refusal.
The integration module is marked cross_os because it depends on git worktree paths, and it names attach_worktree.py literally, so tools/select_tests.py picks it up.

landed_paths uses diff-index --cached against the pre-move HEAD with -z and --no-renames, so staged, fast-forwarded and resolved lands all report both sides of a rename, and unusual path names come through intact.
Moved records the target HEAD before the move on both the start and resume paths, so the rebuild set comes out the same whether the move landed directly or after a --continue.
The plan library loads only when a landed path sits under the plans folder, which keeps pydantic off the a-w path for projects without plans.
_SOURCES builds its patterns from the owning modules' constants (RECEIPTS_DIR, CATALOG_NAME, PLAN_SUFFIX, FREEZES_DIR, plan_stem layout), so a rename in those modules carries through.
Live lines are computed before finish(), so a failed worktree removal still carries them in the AttachError report.

The report formats in all three docs match the code exactly: `live: rebuilt <plans>/<id>/live.js` is refresh_line's f-string, and the `live: warning:` line names `plan.py render <id>` in both warning paths.

The 'move still exits 0' claim holds. refresh_line catches PlanError (the freeze ledger's LedgerError arrives converted by hydrate_frozen), ValueError (which covers pydantic ValidationError) and OSError, and live_lines catches ConfigError, AttachError and ImportError.
The release table's harness 0.79.1 matches plugin.json. The latest tag is v0.7.0, so extending the still-proposed v1.0.0 notes follows the release rule.
The new SKILL bullet sits right after the 'ignored files are deleted with the worktree' bullet, so the one exception is scoped where a reader meets the rule.

The SKILL.md bullet, the module docstring and the code agree on the rebuild trigger set (receipts, freeze ledger entries, plan JSON, DesignEvolution), the 'live: rebuilt' and 'live: warning:' line shapes and the exit code staying 0.
The Moved NamedTuple records the target HEAD in both start() and resume() before any landing step, so staged, --committed and --continue all measure landed paths from the right base.
live_lines runs after clear_state and before finish, so the rebuild happens before the worktree goes, as documented. A failed rebuild is a warning line, never a refusal after the move has landed.
plan_live is imported only when plan paths landed, which keeps a-w free of pydantic. ImportError is caught and reported as a warning.

refresh_line catches PlanError, ValueError and OSError. Since pydantic ValidationError is a ValueError and hydrate_frozen turns LedgerError into PlanError, the realistic plan-load failures are covered.
The rebuild goes to target / plans rather than cfg.path(...), so it hits the checkout the files landed in even when config_root falls back to the main checkout.
refresh_live uses the same gate as plan_render_html.refresh_pip (uses_receipts plus an existing page), so a-w rebuilds live.js exactly when plan.py render would refresh it.
moved_plans imports the pydantic-backed plan library only after a plans path landed, so a-w keeps running without pydantic on moves that touch no plan.
Moved captures the target HEAD before the move in both start() and resume(), so the landed set is right for staged, --committed and --continue moves alike.
The sourced_plans patterns are built from library constants (RECEIPTS_DIR, CATALOG_NAME, PLAN_SUFFIX, FREEZES_DIR) instead of repeating the names as literals.

The integration tests run the real script with a non-default artifacts.plans and cover the staged, --committed, --continue, no-plan and failed-rebuild paths, including a check that an unmoved plan is not rebuilt.
The module docstring, SKILL.md, the README row, the release-note table and line, and the version bump all change together; v1.0.0 has no tag yet, so extending its notes follows the release rule.

The rebuild runs after the move lands and before the worktree is removed, and every failure path (config, git, import, plan load) degrades to a `live: warning:` line naming `plan.py render`, keeping exit code 0.

landed_paths diffs the target index against the pre-move HEAD, so staged, --committed fast-forward and --continue moves share one detection path; the end-to-end tests cover all three modes plus the no-plan and failed-rebuild cases.
The pydantic-dependent plan library is imported lazily, so a-w keeps running without it and an ImportError becomes a warning.
refresh_live mirrors refresh_pip's gate (frozen receipts plan with an existing page), so the attach never writes a live.js plan.py render would not.

minor.name: refresh_live docstring overstates its match with plan.py render
minor.summary: refresh_live says it rebuilds live.js 'when plan.py render would: a frozen receipts plan whose HTML page exists', and the module docstring says it rebuilds 'the way plan.py render does'. render (plan_render_html.refresh_pip) also writes live.js for a frozen receipts plan whose page is missing, through write_pip, which writes the page as well. refresh_live returns None in that case. That behavior is reasonable for an attach, because without a page nothing reloads live.js, but the docstrings describe a wider match than the code has.
fix: Reword the refresh_live docstring to 'Rebuild live.js as plan.py render does for a frozen receipts plan whose HTML page exists; a plan without a page is left for render to write', and change 'the way plan.py render does' in the module docstring to match.

minor.name: A landed HTML page does not trigger a live.js rebuild, although refresh_live gates on the page
minor.summary:
refresh_live (plan_live.py:94-106) rebuilds only when the plan's _PIP.html page exists, so the page is part of what decides whether a target needs live.js. _SOURCES (plan_live.py:28-33) leaves the page out, and test_other_paths_feed_no_plan (tests/lib/test_plan_live.py:96) pins that. Take a frozen receipts plan whose JSON, ledger and receipts are already on the target, with no page there. If the worktree regenerates the missing page (refresh_pip writes the page when it is missing, plan_render_html.py:257-268) and the move lands only that page, a-w rebuilds nothing. The target then shows its new page without live.js and every item reads PENDING, which is the issue #320 symptom this PR fixes.

Also (adv_code): refresh_live rebuilds only when `<id>_*_PIP.html` exists, yet sourced_plans deliberately excludes the page (test_other_paths_feed_no_plan pins `work/plans/0001_Add_operators_PIP.html` as feeding no plan). When the target holds a frozen receipts plan with its receipts but no page (never rendered there, or deleted), and the worktree runs `plan.py render <id>` (refresh_pip falls through to write_pip, writing the page and live.js), the attach moves the page alone; live.js is ignored and discarded with the worktree, and nothing rebuilds it, so the newly landed page reloads a missing live.js.

Attack: Project on main with frozen receipts plan 0001 (plan JSON, ledger freeze entry with records=receipts, a committed receipts/TASK-1.json) but no `work/plans/0001_Sample_PIP.html`; cut a detached worktree, write only `work/plans/0001_Sample_PIP.html` there (what `plan.py render 0001` writes alongside live.js), run `attach_worktree.py main --worktree <wt>`. The page is staged in the target, `pl.sourced_plans(["work/plans/0001_Sample_PIP.html"], "work/plans")` is `[]`, no `live:` line prints, and `work/plans/0001/live.js` is absent in the target.
fix: Add rf"^(\d+)_[^/]*{re.escape(pd.PIP_HTML_SUFFIX)}$" to _SOURCES, move "work/plans/0001_Add_operators_PIP.html" from test_other_paths_feed_no_plan to the test_each_live_source_names_its_plan cases, and add the page to the source lists in the attach_worktree.py docstring, SKILL.md and the release note.
Keep the page out of the sources and say so in the _SOURCES comment and the a-w docs: a page that lands alone gets no rebuild, and the developer runs plan.py render <id>.

Add `rf"^(\d+)_[^/]*{re.escape(pd.PIP_HTML_SUFFIX)}$"` to plan_live._SOURCES and move `work/plans/0001_Add_operators_PIP.html` from test_other_paths_feed_no_plan into test_each_live_source_names_its_plan

minor.name: a-w SKILL omits the page condition and pre-staged paths of the live.js rebuild
minor.summary:
plugins/harness/skills/a-w/SKILL.md:55-59 says live.js is rebuilt 'for every frozen receipts plan whose receipts, freeze ledger entries, plan JSON or DesignEvolution the move landed'. The code applies two more rules. First, plan_live.refresh_live returns None and prints nothing unless the plan's HTML PIP (pd.pip_html_path) exists. Second, attach_worktree.landed_paths diffs the target index against the pre-move HEAD, so paths the target already held staged also count as landed. The module docstring (attach_worktree.py:40-45) states both rules, and docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:265 states the page rule ('with a page'). The skill the agent follows states neither. An agent that sees no `live: rebuilt` line for a moved plan with no page, or an extra line for a plan the worktree never touched, has no text to explain it. The README row (README.md:32) has the same gap: 'for each plan whose receipts, ledger or plan files the move lands'.

Also (skill_package): The module docstring (attach_worktree.py:44) and landed_paths (attach_worktree.py:361-367) count every path the target's index differs on from its pre-move HEAD, including paths the developer had already staged in the target. The new SKILL.md bullet (SKILL.md:55-59) says only plans 'the move landed' get a rebuild. An agent reading the skill cannot account for a 'live: rebuilt' line for a plan the worktree never touched.

Also (overall): landed_paths diffs the target index against the pre-move HEAD (attach_worktree.py:361-367). The module docstring (attach_worktree.py:44) states that paths the target already held staged count as landed. SKILL.md:55-59, the README a-w row and docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:263-268 say only 'whose ... the move landed'. A developer reading the skill will not expect a 'live: rebuilt' line for a plan the worktree never touched but that the target had staged.
fix: In plugins/harness/skills/a-w/SKILL.md:55-59, change 'for every frozen receipts plan whose' to 'for every frozen receipts plan with an HTML page whose', and add after 'the move landed under `artifacts.plans`' the parenthetical '(paths the target already held staged count too)'. In README.md:32, change 'for each plan whose' to 'for each frozen plan with a page whose'.
Append to the SKILL.md:55-59 bullet: '(paths the target already held staged count as landed)', the same wording as the module docstring.
Append '(paths the target already held staged count as landed)' to the SKILL.md bullet at lines 55-59, matching the module docstring.

minor.name: plans_folder activates the config a second time
minor.summary:
plans_folder calls activate(load_config(config_root(target))) only to read artifacts.plans. On the plain-run path load_rules has already activated the same config, so the driver now activates twice, against the project rule that drivers activate once. None of the library code the rebuild calls (plan_live, plan_doc, plan_receipts, evolution_doc, freeze_ledger) reads active(), so the activation does nothing.

Also (skill_package): plans_folder (attach_worktree.py:370-373) turns artifacts.plans into a path prefix with only a backslash swap and strip('/'). The schema's relPath allows './docs/plans' or 'docs/./plans', and git diff-index paths never carry those segments, so no landed path matches. The rebuild then quietly does nothing and prints no live: warning line, even though the docstring and SKILL.md promise a rebuild or a warning. review_adversarial.py:85 already builds the same prefix with posixpath.normpath.

Also (adv_code): plans_folder only swaps backslashes and strips slashes, so `artifacts.plans` = `./work/plans` (accepted by the relPath schema pattern, and resolved fine by `active().path(...)` everywhere else) yields the prefix `./work/plans/`. The landed paths git reports never start with `./`, so moved_plans returns no plan ids and the attach prints neither `live: rebuilt` nor a `live: warning:` line. The same applies to `work//plans` or `work/plans/.`. The developer gets a page with no live.js and no hint to run `plan.py render`.

Attack: Build the tests/skills/test_attach_worktree_plan_live.py `repos` fixture but with `make_project(config={"artifacts": {"plans": "./work/plans"}}, ...)`, write the TASK-1 receipt in the worktree and run `attach_worktree.py main --worktree <wt>`. Probe result: rc 0, the receipt is staged in the target, the output has no `live:` line at all, and `work/plans/0001/live.js` does not exist. The same run with `work/plans` prints `live: rebuilt work/plans/0001/live.js` and writes the file.
fix: Read the key without activating: cfg = load_config(config_root(target)) at line 372.
Or activate once in attach() for both the start and resume paths, and have plans_folder read active().artifacts.plans.

Return posixpath.normpath(cfg.artifacts.plans.replace('\\', '/')).strip('/') in plans_folder, matching review_adversarial.py:85; plan_live.sourced_plans re-strips the value it receives, so passing the normalized string through keeps both sides in agreement.

Normalise in plans_folder with `posixpath.normpath(cfg.artifacts.plans.replace('\\', '/')).strip('/')` (the form review_adversarial.py already uses), and add a parametrized case with `./work/plans` to tests/skills/test_attach_worktree_plan_live.py
Apply the same normpath in plan_live.sourced_plans so its own prefix matches for any caller

minor.name: live_lines lets an OSError escape after the move landed
minor.summary:
The attach module docstring (lines 40-45) and live_lines (lines 404-405) promise that a failed rebuild is a 'live: warning:' line, never a refusal. live_lines catches only (ConfigError, AttachError, ImportError) around moved_plans, but plans_folder -> config_root -> project_root/main_worktree runs git through harness_lib.project, whose timeout raises TimeoutError (an OSError), and run_git can raise OSError when git cannot launch. Such an error escapes attach() after resolve.clear_state and before finish(): main() does not catch it, so the run ends in a traceback with the move landed, the worktree not removed and no report lines printed. refresh_line already lists OSError for the per-plan step.

Also (overall): The live_lines docstring (attach_worktree.py:401-406) says a failure is a warning line and never a refusal. Its except clause (line 409) catches only ConfigError, AttachError and ImportError. moved_plans -> plans_folder -> config_root runs project_root/main_worktree, whose git call can raise TimeoutError (an OSError, harness_lib/project.py:32). On the --continue path load_rules never ran, so this is the first config lookup of the run. An escaped exception leaves attach() (line 435) after clear_state and before finish. The landed move's report, with its backup sha and undo lines, is never printed, the worktree is not removed, and the run exits 1 with a traceback.

Also (overall): refresh_live writes to write_live(plans_dir, plan.plan_id) (plan_live.py:106), which is the id inside the plan JSON. refresh_line builds its report as f"live: rebuilt {plans}/{plan_id}/{written.name}" (attach_worktree.py:398) from the id that sourced_plans parsed out of the file or folder name. If a plan file's prefix and its plan_id disagree, the line names a folder that was not written, and live.js lands in a folder the page does not read.
fix: Add OSError to the except tuple in live_lines (line 409): except (ConfigError, AttachError, ImportError, OSError) as exc.
Add OSError to the except tuple at attach_worktree.py:409.
Wrap the live_lines call in attach() with a broad except Exception that turns any error into the generic 'live: warning: live.js not rebuilt (...)' line, so the move's report always reaches finish().
Build the line from the returned path: f"live: rebuilt {written.relative_to(target).as_posix()}".
Or have refresh_live write under the plan_id argument it was asked to refresh, so the reported folder and the written folder cannot differ.

minor.name: write-plan README's list of live.js rebuilders is now stale
minor.summary:
plugins/harness/skills/write-plan/README.md:84-85 says 'after a pull, `PLAN render <id>` rebuilds it', and lines 124-126 list the steps that rebuild live.js and keep the plan folder's .gitignore line: 'record, freeze, render, `evolution_api`'. With this PR the a-w attach also rebuilds live.js in the target. It calls plan_live.write_live, which runs _ignore_live, so it also creates or appends `<plans>/<id>/.gitignore` there. That write can leave an unstaged or untracked file in the target next to a staged move, and the a-w SKILL bullet (SKILL.md:55-59) does not mention it either. The plan lifecycle README is where a developer looks to learn when live.js comes back, and it now misses the attach.

Also (skill_package): The rebuild goes through plan_live.write_live (plan_live.py:67-74), whose _ignore_live creates or appends <plans>/<id>/.gitignore in the target. write-plan README.md:125 lists every driver that rebuilds live.js and adds that line (record, freeze, render, evolution_api) and omits a-w. README.md:85 names only 'PLAN render <id>' as the way to rebuild after a pull. Neither the a-w SKILL.md nor its docstring says the attach can leave an unstaged .gitignore change in the target outside the move's staged result.
fix: In plugins/harness/skills/write-plan/README.md:125, change '(record, freeze, render, `evolution_api`)' to '(record, freeze, render, `evolution_api`, and an a-w attach that lands the plan's files)'. At line 85, append 'an a-w attach rebuilds it in the target'. Optionally, add to the a-w SKILL.md bullet that the rebuild may add the `live.js` line to the plan folder's `.gitignore` in the target.
Add a-w to the list at write-plan README.md:125 ('record, freeze, render, evolution_api, and an a-w attach that lands plan files') and note at README.md:85 that an a-w attach rebuilds live.js itself.
Add a clause to the a-w SKILL.md:55-59 bullet saying the rebuild may also create or extend the plan folder's .gitignore in the target as an unstaged change.

minor.name: Test module docstring leaves out the HTML page condition and the already-staged rule
minor.summary: The docstring says a-w rebuilds live.js 'for every frozen receipts plan whose receipts, freeze ledger, plan JSON or DesignEvolution the move wrote'. The code (plan_live.refresh_live, attach_worktree.py:40-45) also requires the plan's HTML page to exist, and it counts paths the target already held staged as landed. The fixtures include a page, so the tests pass, but the prose contract does not match what they exercise. The already-staged rule has no test.
fix: Change lines 4-6 to say 'every frozen receipts plan with an HTML page whose ... the move landed (paths the target already held staged count)'.
Optionally add a staged-move test: stage a receipt for plan 0001 in the target before the attach, move an unrelated worktree file, and assert `live: rebuilt work/plans/0001/live.js`.

minor.name: The integration fixture ignores every per-plan .gitignore and so never checks the target's working tree after a rebuild
minor.summary: _IGNORES (tests/skills/test_attach_worktree_plan_live.py:36) adds 'work/plans/**/.gitignore' plus a root 'live.js' rule. Real projects track the per-plan .gitignore that write_live keeps (plan_live.py:58-64; D9 says no project adds an ignore line). Because the fixture ignores those files, the tests never see that a rebuild can create or edit <plans>/<id>/.gitignore in the target as an unstaged change. No test asserts what the target's working tree looks like after the attach, so a regression in that side effect would go unnoticed.
fix: Drop the '**/.gitignore' and root 'live.js' lines from _IGNORES and assert the target's 'git status --porcelain' after a rebuild (for example, the plan folder's .gitignore shows as untracked or modified, and live.js stays ignored).
Keep the fixture and add a comment explaining why the per-plan .gitignore is ignored, plus one test that pins the target-side .gitignore state.

minor.name: Stopped attach is not checked for an early live.js rebuild
minor.summary: test_continue_rebuilds_live_js_after_a_resolution only checks that the first attach exits 2. It never asserts that the stopped run printed no `live:` line and left no live.js in the target. If the rebuild ran at the stop as well as at --continue, the test would still pass, so it does not pin the contract that the rebuild runs only after a successful move (module docstring lines 4-6; attach_worktree.py:40-45).
fix: Keep the stopped run's CompletedProcess. Assert `stopped.returncode == 2`, `not any(line.startswith("live:") for line in stopped.stdout.splitlines())` and `_live(main, "0001") is None` before the resolution step.
